title: What If You Skipped 10,000 Steps? The Number Was Marketing

scenes.text: What if 10,000 steps a day was never a medical target? It started as a product name.
In 1965, a Japanese company sold a pedometer called Manpo-kei, which means 10,000 steps meter.
A Harvard researcher says the name was a marketing tool, not science.
A study followed 16,741 women, average age 72, with step counters.
Women averaging 4,400 steps a day had a lower risk of death than those averaging 2,700.
The benefit leveled off around 7,500 steps. How fast they walked made no difference.
